Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

# Surf's Up, Pelican

An animated, **non-interactive** 3D vignette: a pelican surfing a breaking wave,
built with HTML and Three.js. Just open the page and watch — there are no
controls. The camera drifts slowly on its own and the loop runs forever.

## What's in the scene

- A procedural pelican (body, balancing wings, tail, legs, head with eyes,
  long beak and a wobbling throat pouch) riding a coral surfboard.
- Animated ocean swells, a breaking wave with a foam crest, spray particles,
  a stern wake, drifting clouds, distant gulls, sun and gradient sky.

## Run it

```sh
npm install
npx serve .        # or: python3 -m http.server
```

Then open `index.html` (entry point; code lives in `main.js` as ES modules).

## Notes

- Imports `three` by package name — no CDN URLs, no import maps.
- All visuals are generated in code (no external assets), so the packaged page
  runs offline with no network requests and uses no storage APIs.
- Packaging check: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null`
  must succeed.

Done. I built an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican page in the current directory.

What it is: a looping 3D vignette ([index.html](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-high-20261017-090728/work/index.html), code in [main.js](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-high-20261017-090728/work/main.js), plus [README.md](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-spark-1.3-mc-high-20261017-090728/work/README.md)). A procedural pelican — balancing flapping wings, wagging tail, head that looks around, long beak with a wobbling throat pouch — rides a coral surfboard on bobbing ocean swells in front of a breaking wave with a foam crest, spray particles, wake puffs, drifting clouds, gulls, sun and gradient sky. The camera drifts cinematically on its own; there are no controls or interactions besides window resize.

Packaging-safe: `three` is imported by package name (no CDN, no import maps), every visual is generated in code with zero external assets, and nothing uses network or storage APIs. `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` succeeds.
